limitations: Coverage/provenance verification only: no signal, outcome, or performance metric is computed.
A matching digest proves the recorded candle series reproduces from the current public venue API bytes; it does not prove the venue never revised history.
Execution-price checks compare recorded entry/exit candle open/close values to refetched rows with tolerance 0; they prove price provenance only, not that the trades were executable at those prices.

Funding row counts are reported separately from the candle digests because OKX publishes a rolling ~3-month funding history: rows older than the retention boundary cannot be refetched even though they remain persisted in the target artifact's settlement and selection evidence.

Funding settlement checks compare each recorded venue/side/settlement-timestamp rate, interval, 8h normalization and cash flow against refetched rows with tolerance 0. Settlements older than a venue's refetched history are labelled outside_retention only when the fetch itself proves truncation (OKX stop_reason=page_not_full); they are not counted as matched source observations.

Daily dispersion is recomputed from refetched 1h Hyperliquid + 8h OKX funding rows with an independent time-weighted-mean/population-std implementation. Dates whose OKX funding window predates the current rolling ~3-month retention are labelled outside_retention (never silently matched) when the refetch proves truncation; their persisted values remain in the immutable anchor artifact.

The prior-90-date 80th-percentile threshold, type-7 quantile, current-date exclusion and the top-10% tail selection are re-derived from the persisted daily dispersion series, so they prove the arithmetic signal rule exactly but inherit any source limitation of the dispersion inputs they consume.
Selection-window reproducibility checks every recorded observation's original rate against a refetched venue row (tolerance 0) and recomputes the window dispersion from those observations.
Contract identity remains underlying-symbol-mapped candidate level.
